scope.lane: C.7 per-request cache evidence and estimated history cost

findings.title: Update four cost-command fixtures for measured reads and known write prices
findings.classification: stale test fixtures under the intended C.7 contract
findings.impact: The production change leaves four existing cost-command tests with cache-output assertions that cannot be satisfied by their supplied records. Their fixtures omit current cache-read evidence, so the summary has no accounted requests and the miss comparison has no comparable pair. The write-only miss fixture also omits the write price needed to compute its expected dollar estimate. A focused integration run including this suite must classify and repair these fixtures before this change can be approved.
findings.trigger: Inspect the tiny-cache, cache-unpriced, write-only miss, and model-switch fixtures in the unchanged costCommand.test.ts. They supply prompt-only or write-only records, yet expect a cache hit rate, positive extra cost, or a model-change cache notice.

evidence.note: Omitted cacheReadTokens becomes cacheReadReported:false in every newly recorded history entry.
Summary inclusion requires current read evidence; a write-only record cannot prove a measured zero read.
A miss comparison requires read evidence. Positive writes additionally require measured write evidence and a write price at line 205.
The actual report renderer omits the cache section when both accounted request count and miss count are zero.
tiny-cache supplies no read category; assertions at lines 180 and 183 nevertheless require a positive cache estimate.
cache-unpriced supplies only a write category; line 233 still expects a measured 0% cache-read hit rate.
The write-only miss records at lines 346/348 omit reads and the fixture catalogue omits a write price. Lines 352, 354 and 356 expect a 0% hit rate, 100,000 overlapping tokens and $0.2700.
The model-switch records at lines 444/446 omit reads; lines 450/451 nevertheless require a cache section and its model-change notice.

findings.suggestedFix: Retain root-owned actual failures and classify these existing fixtures before editing. Supply explicit numeric read zero where a test intends a measured miss. Supply a known write price or a fixture without an observed write bucket where it intends a priced miss. Preserve the tiny-cost, unknown-read-price and model-change purposes and their meaningful numerical assertions. Keep the original 13 counterexample bodies unchanged.
findings.disposition: open; root acknowledged all four fixtures and plans an actual serial failure/classification followed by contract-preserving fixture updates
findings.confidence: high from the supplied fixture fields, recording/filter conditions and actual cache report renderer

coverage.rawNormalization: Inspected all of provider/response/usage.ts and its tests. Valid finite nonnegative native or nested raw category values, including zero, produce presence evidence before billing defaults. Missing/invalid categories produce false. Existing exclusive native input, inclusive compatible input, output and total-token arithmetic remains unchanged. Inspected Anthropic, Google, Bedrock and Responses usage mappings, including within-request stream merging, to verify absence is preserved before the canonical normalizer.
coverage.recordingAndLegacy: Inspected all of usageTelemetry.ts and usage/model.ts. Canonical false flags refuse inference from zero-filled counts; direct finite nonnegative numeric categories, including zero, are measured. Explicit true without a numeric category cannot invent evidence. Current category flags remain separate from historical reportedCache. Older positive category counts remain evidence; sticky-only legacy zeros remain unknown. Price edits retain destination metadata without promoting current absence.
coverage.summariesAndContinuity: Inspected all of cacheWaste.ts. Summaries include only measured read requests. Missing read evidence and unpriced observed writes break miss comparison continuity. Context resets, usage gaps and damaged-history recovery gap placeholders prevent comparisons across lost requests. Legacy-to-attributed identity boundaries remain fenced, and the bounded history size/merge behavior remains intact.
coverage.pricesAndEstimates: Inspected captured-rate identity and actual cost-model consumers. Weighted ordinary-input and write prices correctly account for all-write and mixed-write premiums, while observed unpriced writes withhold a dollar miss. Captured unknown prices are not replenished from a later catalogue. Count overlap remains explicitly an estimate; the changed turn-end wording says estimated overlapping tokens, and the idle label says possible expiry.
coverage.persistenceAndReopen: Inspected all of usage/snapshot.ts and the recovery path. Optional category evidence accepts booleans only, retains absent legacy fields, and survives strict decode/copy/freeze/reopen. Legacy history equality includes the new flags so distinct evidence is not collapsed. Corrupt evidence is rejected, with tolerant recovery retaining independently valid billing and a usage-gap placeholder rather than joining history across the loss.
coverage.canonicalProducers: Read actual main-tree turn/step.ts:436-466, btwCommandRuntime.ts:84-98, and session/store/usage.ts:29-70. They spread the canonical normalized records without dropping presence. Foreground prompt/context admission retains its existing validated measurement/identity contract; auxiliary requests retain affectsContext:false. No caller plumbing repair or replay/context authority change is required.
coverage.tests: Inspected all four frozen test files and both final patches. Nineteen presence cases cover raw absence, empty details, write-only records, explicit zero, legacy sticky-only records, reset/gap boundaries, write premiums, unknown captured prices, later catalogues, invalid raw reads, direct numeric zero and partial categories. Provider body/stream normalization and persistence-corruption controls retain existing numerical assertions. Reconstructed the original counterexample source from tests.patch and confirmed its exact SHA-256 and unchanged prefix in the current file.
coverage.existingTestIntegration: Inspected the actual downstream cost model/report and relevant existing costCommand.test.ts fixtures. The four stale integration fixtures are reported above; this report does not infer passing broader validation.
coverage.boundaries: Read-only product/test review. Only this requested receipt was written. No tests, builds, gates, NormProof, provider/native execution, git mutations, language-server indexing or delegation. No other review or architecture approval was adopted.
